Here is a summary of the passage:

To measure the efficiency of an algorithm, computer scientists analyze running time as a function of the input size. They prioritize calculating "upper bounds"—the maximum amount of time an algorithm will take—because this provides a necessary performance guarantee for users, ensuring they know the worst-case scenario for how long a program will run.
